text:
hao: Quick sync: I'm iterating on a 'slab packer' for Dedicated pools. It issues fractional slabs (1/8,1/4) and packs them into physical GPU leases. Need feedback on operator boundary and safety checks.

lex: Nice. Operator sees only physical leases, right? No per-slab ops?

hao: Correct. Operator gets periodic intent docs: desired physical counts + labels. Packer handles splits/merges locally.

ram: Main concerns: memory isolation and tail latency when many slabs share a card. How do you detect and react to contention?

hao: We track a per-physical contention score (mem pressure + queued requests). If it crosses threshold the packer stops admitting to that node and returns throttle_until in admit. Also can proactively migrate slabs off.

tara: Persistence model? Restart should be safe.

hao: Slab manifests persisted to etcd. We use epoched lease versions for CAS during merge to avoid races. On restart packer rebuilds state from etcd and re-queries operator.

lex: API example? Keep it tiny.

hao: POST /admit {tenant, slabs, qos} => {admitted, lease_id, slab_units, throttle_until} plus POST /release and GET /usage.

ram: Rollout: canary tenants + opt-in routing. Start with no overcommit, then slowly enable conservative overcommit after stability window.

tara: Observability: slab churn, pack_ratio, per-physical contention, admit latency. Add alert if pack_ratio > 0.6 and contention > 0.2.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started for slab-packer eu-west-1  build#4901

hao: I'll draft short RFC with API shapes, operator intent schema, and a canary checklist. Thanks for quick feedback. End.
